chunks: Warn the people of that Day when the punishment would be inflicted upon them. Then will the wicked say: 'O our Lord, give us respite a while more. We shall heed Your call and follow the apostles.' (But they will be told): 'Are you not those who used to swear: There is no reverse for us?'
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the irony of the disbelievers' last-minute repentance, noting that their previous oath of permanence ('you would never be destroyed') reflects a deep-seated arrogance that delayed their acceptance of the truth. The phrase 'follow the messengers' is often interpreted as a general acknowledgment rather than true submission, emphasizing that the opportunity for sincere faith was lost during their lifetime. This scene serves as a warning against procrastination in spiritual matters, a theme frequently discussed by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai in *Al-Mizan*.
